title: CLAUDE.md

title: Mizer
code: library(mizer)  # 1. Create model parameters from a species data frame params <- newMultispeciesParams(species_params, interaction)  # 2. Find the steady state (sets initial values) params <- steady(params)  # 3. Calibrate to observed biomasses / yields params <- calibrateBiomass(params)  # adjusts kappa params <- matchBiomasses(params)    # adjusts R_max per species params <- matchGrowth(params)       # adjusts h per species  # 4. Tune density-dependent reproduction params <- setBevertonHolt(params, reproduction_level = 0.25)  # 5. Project forward in time sim <- project(params, t_max = 20, effort = 1)  # 6. Analyse results plot(sim) getBiomass(sim) getYield(sim) plotSpectra(sim)

Triggers: analyse--plot: Analyse visualise results mizer simulation state MizerParams object. Use whenever user wants extract, summarise, plot size spectra, biomass, yield, SSB, abundance, feeding level, mortality, diet, trophic level, community indicators, growth curves, plankton resource — including comparing two simulations animating spectra time. Prefer built-mizer functions described writing custom extraction ggplot code. build-multispecies-model: Build calibrated multi-species mizer model species-parameter data frame. Use whenever user wants create MizerParams object newMultispeciesParams(), set interaction matrix fishing gears, bring model steady state steady(), calibrate/match observed biomasses, yields, growth (calibrateBiomass, matchBiomasses, matchGrowth, calibrateYield, setBevertonHolt). Follow ordered workflow rather guessing parameters writing dynamics hand. calibrate-model: Bring mizer model steady state calibrate observed data. Use whenever user wants find steady state (steady, projectToSteady, steadySingleSpecies), match modelled biomass, yield, growth observations (calibrateBiomass, matchBiomasses, calibrateYield, matchGrowth), set level density-dependent reproduction (setBevertonHolt), diagnose model settle reproduce observed values. change-parameters: Change parameters existing mizer model correctly. Use whenever user wants modify species parameters, size-dependent rates, fishing, resource, interactions — especially unsure accessor use: given_species_params() vs species_params(), changing species parameter vs setting rate array directly (setSearchVolume, setPredKernel, setParams…), gear_params() vs resource setters. Follow rules avoid changes silently fail propagate get overwritten. extend-mizer: Extend customise mizer’s dynamics — add external food/mortality, replace built-rate calculation, add new ecosystem component. Use whenever user wants custom encounter/growth/mortality/reproduction formulation (setRateFunction), background food predation source (setExtEncounter, setExtMort), new dynamical pool like detritus carrion (setComponent), asks make mizer something standard setters cover. run-simulation: Project mizer model forward time set fishing-effort scenarios. Use whenever user wants run simulation project(), specify constant time-varying fishing effort, choose projection method time step, run new steady state change, continue existing MizerSim, set scenario comparisons. extracting plotting results, see analyse--plot skill. set--fishing: Set change fishing mizer model — gears, selectivity curves, catchability, effort. Use whenever user wants define fishing gears, choose configure selectivity function (knife_edge, sigmoid_length, double_sigmoid_length, sigmoid_weight), set gear catches species, change catchability, set baseline fishing effort setFishing() gear_params data frame. skill’s directory may also hold NOTES.md recording earlier work project found. title: Celtic Sea Status Quo Model
text: Creating model representing average state Celtic Sea 2012 2024. Composed 15 species: herring (Clupea harengus), cod (Gadus morhua), haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus), whiting (Merlangius merlangus), blue whiting (Micromesistius poutassou), hake (Merluccius merluccius), monkfish (Lophius piscatorius), horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus), mackerel (Scomber scombrus), plaice (Pleuronectes platessa), megrim (Lepidorhombus whiffiagonis), sole (Solea solea), boarfish (Capros aper), dragonet (Callionymus spp.), red gurnard (Chelidonicthys cuculus). Data includes: life_history parameters (l_mat age_mat calculated DATRAS data; w_max LWR Fishbase); landing distributions form STECF; survey size distribution age length distribution data DATRAS; Stomach contents data; Biomass estimates, yield estimates, interaction matrix, diet matrix Lauria (2016). Assign species parameters life history data

Gurnards[num_cols] * 0.37 Red_gurnard$Group.name<-"Red gurnard" Other_Gurnards[num_cols] <- Gurnards[num_cols] * 0.63 Boarfish[num_cols]<- Boarfish[num_cols] * 0.97 Boarfish$Group.name<-"Boarfish" addCatch(model_non_int, landings= catch_distribution,                               fishing_dead_biomass=fishing_deaths,                               survey= survey_length_distribution)  # Steady model model_non_int <- model_non_int %>%     steadySingleSpecies() %>%     matchBiomasses() %>%     steadySingleSpecies() %>%     matchBiomasses()%>%     steadySingleSpecies() %>%     matchBiomasses()%>%     steadySingleSpecies() %>%     matchBiomasses()%>%     steadySingleSpecies() %>%     matchBiomasses()  params<-model_non_int sps<-species_params(model_non_int) initial_Eiw<-array(dim=length(sps$species)) for(i in 1:length(sps$species)){     initial_Eiw[i]<-getExtEncounter(params)[i,1]/(w(params)[1]^sp[i,]$n)} sps$Eiw<-initial_Eiw species_params(model_non_int)<-sps  #set the spawning time, spawning concentration and mu mortality of species to predetermined values.  #spawning_mort<-tuneEcopath( #    model_non_int,  #    catch = text: far fish infinite maximum intake metabolic cost, convenient believable. setFeedingLevels() introduces feeding level \(f\) (fraction maximum rate fish eats) critical feeding level \(f_c\) (grow ) solving encounter rate \(E\), maximum intake \(h\) metabolic loss \(k_s\) produce : \[E=E_r\frac{f}{\alpha(f-f_c)(1-f)},\qquad   h = \frac{E_r}{\alpha(f-f_c)},\qquad   k_s = E_r\frac{f_c}{f-f_c}.\] point solving way energy available growth reproduction, \(E_r\), held fixed. fish now realistic physiology, grow exactly , size-distribution fit stage 2 disturbed. Eight nine species get conventional \(f = 0.6\), \(f_c = 0.2\). Whiting gets \(f = 0.8406\), \(f_c = 0.2802\), reason worth setting , turns property formulae easy miss. Substituting \(h\) back consumption rate \(f\,h\,w^n\) gives \[\text{consumption} = \frac{E_r}{\alpha\left(1 - f_c/f\right)},   \qquad k_s = E_r\,\frac{f_c/f}{1 - f_c/f},\] depend \(f\) \(f_c\) ratio. code: # Relative difference between the yield a little above and a little below the # current F. Positive means the peak is above F_cur, negative that it is below. side <- function(params, sp, F_cur, d = 1.25) {     y <- suppressMessages(getYieldVsF(params, sp,                                       F_range = c(F_cur / d, F_cur * d)))     lo <- y$yield[which.min(abs(y$F - F_cur / d))]     hi <- y$yield[which.min(abs(y$F - F_cur * d))]     (hi - lo) / max(hi, lo, 1e-30) }  set_rl <- function(params, sp, rl) {     setBevertonHolt(params, reproduction_level = setNames(rl, sp)) }  tune <- function(params, sp, F_cur, rl_lo = 0.01, rl_hi = 0.99,                  steps = 6, tol = 0.02) {     u2rl <- function(u) 1 - exp(-u)     u_lo <- -log(1 - rl_lo)     u_hi <- -log(1 - rl_hi)     s_lo <- side(set_rl(params, sp, rl_lo), sp, F_cur)     if (s_lo >= 0) return(list(rl = rl_lo, side = s_lo, status = "at lower bound"))     s_hi <- side(set_rl(params, sp, rl_hi), sp, F_cur)     if (s_hi <= 0) return(list(rl = rl_hi, side = s_hi, status = "at upper bound"))     for (i in seq_len(steps)) {         u <- (u_lo + u_hi) / 2         s <- side(set_rl(params, sp, u2rl(u)), sp, F_cur)         if (abs(s) < tol) return(list(rl = u2rl(u), side = s, status = "converged"))         if (s < 0) u_lo <- u else u_hi <- u     }     u <- (u_lo + u_hi) / 2     list(rl = u2rl(u), side = side(set_rl(params, sp, u2rl(u)), sp, F_cur),          status = "bisected") } params <- psr  # The target for each species: its FMSY where the data give one. Plaice has # none, so it falls back to the F the model says it currently experiences. # With effort = 1 the fully-selected F equals the catchability, and we want the # *fitted* catchabilities from the model, not the starting values in `gp`. gpf <- gear_params(params) |> filter(gear == "commercial") Ftarget <- setNames(species_params(params)$FMSY, species_params(params)$species) Ftarget[is.na(Ftarget)] <- setNames(gpf$catchability, gpf$species)[is.na(Ftarget)]  res <- list() for (sweep in 1:2) {     for (sp in names(Ftarget)) {         r <- tune(params, sp, Ftarget[[sp]])         params <- set_rl(params, sp, r$rl)         res[[sp]] <- r     } } do.call(rbind, lapply(res, as.data.frame)) t(vapply(names(F_target), function(sp) peak(params, sp, F_target[[sp]]), numeric(2)))

code: species_params(p)$production_observed <- getSomaticProduction(p) pm <- matchCatch(p, catch = catch) # Multinomial negative log likelihood of the observed catch size distributions # given the model, per species and gear, reported as an excess over the # saturated (best possible) value and divided by the number of fish so that it # is comparable across species and across models. catch_nll <- function(params, catch) {     sp <- species_params(params)     fm <- getFMortGear(params)     out <- NULL     for (i in seq_len(nrow(sp))) {         s <- sp$species[i]         w <- w(params); dw <- dw(params)         for (g in unique(catch$gear[catch$species == s])) {             obs <- catch[catch$species == s & catch$gear == g &                              !is.na(catch$catch), ]             if (nrow(obs) == 0) next             cw <- fm[g, i, ] * initialN(params)[i, ]             edges <- sp$a[i] * c(obs$length, max(obs$length + obs$dl))^sp$b[i]             cum <- c(0, cumsum(cw * dw))             lo <- w[1] - dw[1] / 2; hi <- max(w + dw / 2)             F_at <- approx(c(lo, w + dw / 2), cum,                            xout = pmin(pmax(edges, lo), hi), rule = 2)$y             prob <- diff(F_at); prob <- prob / sum(prob)             k <- obs$catch             phat <- k / sum(k)             out <- rbind(out, data.frame(                 species = s, gear = g, n = sum(k),                 excess = (-sum(k * log(pmax(prob, 1e-12))) +                               sum(k[k > 0] * log(phat[k > 0]))) / sum(k)))         }     }     out } nll <- catch_nll(pm, catch) nll |> arrange(gear, species) |>     mutate(excess = round(excess, 4)) |>     kable(row.names = FALSE,           caption = "Excess negative log likelihood per fish. code: # Multinomial negative log likelihood of the observed catch size distributions # given the model, per species and gear, reported as an excess over the # saturated (best possible) value and divided by the number of fish so that it # is comparable across species and across models. catch_nll <- function(params, catch) {     sp <- species_params(params)     fm <- getFMortGear(params)     out <- NULL     for (i in seq_len(nrow(sp))) {         s <- sp$species[i]         w <- w(params); dw <- dw(params)         for (g in unique(catch$gear[catch$species == s])) {             obs <- catch[catch$species == s & catch$gear == g &                              !is.na(catch$catch), ]             if (nrow(obs) == 0) next             cw <- fm[g, i, ] * initialN(params)[i, ]             edges <- sp$a[i] * c(obs$length, max(obs$length + obs$dl))^sp$b[i]             cum <- c(0, cumsum(cw * dw))             lo <- w[1] - dw[1] / 2; hi <- max(w + dw / 2)             F_at <- approx(c(lo, w + dw / 2), cum,                            xout = pmin(pmax(edges, lo), hi), rule = 2)$y             prob <- diff(F_at); prob <- prob / sum(prob)             k <- obs$catch             phat <- k / sum(k)             out <- rbind(out, data.frame(                 species = s, gear = g, n = sum(k),                 excess = (-sum(k * log(pmax(prob, 1e-12))) +                               sum(k[k > 0] * log(phat[k > 0]))) / sum(k)))         }     }     out } nll <- catch_nll(pm, catch) nll |> arrange(gear, species) |>     mutate(excess = round(excess, 4)) |>     kable(row.names = FALSE,           caption = "Excess negative log likelihood per fish. Zero would be a perfect fit to the raw 1 cm bins.")

code: setFeedingLevelInteracting <- function(params, f_new) {     f_old <- getFeedingLevel(params)     sp <- species_params(params)$species     if (is.null(names(f_new))) names(f_new) <- sp     for (s in names(f_new)) {         i <- match(s, sp)         cc <- (1 - f_old[i, ]) / (1 - f_new[[s]])         sv <- search_vol(params); sv[i, ] <- sv[i, ] * cc         search_vol(params) <- sv         ee <- ext_encounter(params); ee[i, ] <- ee[i, ] * cc         ext_encounter(params) <- ee         E <- getEncounter(params)         im <- intake_max(params)         im[i, ] <- E[i, ] * (1 - f_new[[s]]) / f_new[[s]]         intake_max(params) <- im     }     params } f <- setNames(rep(0.6, 9), species_params(psr)$species) f[["Herring"]] <- 0.94 psr <- setFeedingLevelInteracting(psr, f) set_link <- function(params, pred, prey, lambda) {     mort_old <- getPredMort(params)     enc_old  <- getEncounter(params)     inter <- interaction_matrix(params)     inter[pred, prey] <- inter[pred, prey] * lambda     interaction_matrix(params) <- inter     # Encounter first: predation mortality carries a factor (1 - f) and so     # depends on the encounter rate. Restoring the mortality first would bake a     # spurious external mortality into every prey species.     ext_encounter(params) <- ext_encounter(params) +         (enc_old - getEncounter(params))     ext_mort(params) <- ext_mort(params) + (mort_old - getPredMort(params))     params } allsp <- species_params(psr)$species psr <- set_link(psr, "Whiting", allsp, 0.65) psr <- set_link(psr, "Cod", allsp, 0.01)

code: # Relative difference between the yield a little above and a little below the # current F. Positive means the peak is above F_cur, negative that it is below. side <- function(params, sp, F_cur, d = 1.25) {     y <- suppressMessages(getYieldVsF(params, sp,                                       F_range = c(F_cur / d, F_cur * d)))     lo <- y$yield[which.min(abs(y$F - F_cur / d))]     hi <- y$yield[which.min(abs(y$F - F_cur * d))]     (hi - lo) / max(hi, lo, 1e-30) }  set_rl <- function(params, sp, rl) {     setBevertonHolt(params, reproduction_level = setNames(rl, sp)) }  tune <- function(params, sp, F_cur, rl_lo = 0.01, rl_hi = 0.99,                  steps = 6, tol = 0.02) {     u2rl <- function(u) 1 - exp(-u)     u_lo <- -log(1 - rl_lo)     u_hi <- -log(1 - rl_hi)     s_lo <- side(set_rl(params, sp, rl_lo), sp, F_cur)     if (s_lo >= 0) return(list(rl = rl_lo, side = s_lo, status = "at lower bound"))     s_hi <- side(set_rl(params, sp, rl_hi), sp, F_cur)     if (s_hi <= 0) return(list(rl = rl_hi, side = s_hi, status = "at upper bound"))     for (i in seq_len(steps)) {         u <- (u_lo + u_hi) / 2         s <- side(set_rl(params, sp, u2rl(u)), sp, F_cur)         if (abs(s) < tol) return(list(rl = u2rl(u), side = s, status = "converged"))         if (s < 0) u_lo <- u else u_hi <- u     }     u <- (u_lo + u_hi) / 2     list(rl = u2rl(u), side = side(set_rl(params, sp, u2rl(u)), sp, F_cur),          status = "bisected") } params <- psr  # The target for each species: its FMSY where the data give one. Plaice has # none, so it falls back to the F the model says it currently experiences. # With effort = 1 the fully-selected F equals the catchability, and we want the # *fitted* catchabilities from the model, not the starting values in `gp`. gpf <- gear_params(params) |> filter(gear == "commercial") Ftarget <- setNames(species_params(params)$FMSY, species_params(params)$species) Ftarget[is.na(Ftarget)] <- setNames(gpf$catchability, gpf$species)[is.na(Ftarget)]  We set the reproduction levels to values found through tuning to ensure the yield curves peak near $F_{MSY}$. code: library(mizerEcopath)  # Collapse celtic_params to one gear per species. make_single_gear <- function() {     params <- celtic_params     gp <- gear_params(params)     keep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(gp, gp$species), function(g) {         row <- g[which.max(g$yield_observed), , drop = FALSE]         row$gear <- "total"         row$yield_observed <- sum(g$yield_observed)         row     }))     rownames(keep) <- paste(keep$species, keep$gear, sep = ", ")     gear_params(params) <- keep     initial_effort(params) <- 1     params }  # Expected catch in each 1-cm length bin: the integral of the catch density # N*F over the bin. We use the same piecewise-linear interpolation of the # density that matchCatch()'s likelihood uses internally, so that the # synthetic data is *self-consistent* with the model. (A cruder histogram — # assigning each weight bin to floor(length) — disagrees with the likelihood's # integration by a few percent, and because the mortality-diffusion valley is # so flat that small discrepancy is enough to shift the fitted mortality # substantially. Self-consistent binning is what lets a perfect catch recover # the truth.) model_catch_rate <- function(params, species, bins) {     sp <- species_params(params); s <- which(sp$species == species); sps <- sp[s, ]     w <- params@w     dens <- approxfun(w, params@initial_n[s, ] * getFMort(params)[s, ], rule = 2)     vapply(bins, function(L) {         lo <- sps$a * L^sps$b; hi <- sps$a * (L + 1)^sps$b         grid <- sort(unique(c(w[w > lo & w < hi], lo, hi)))         v <- dens(grid); sum(diff(grid) * (head(v, -1) + tail(v, -1)) / 2)     }, numeric(1)) }  # Generate model catch data over 1-cm bins (integer counts summing to ~n_total). model_catch_data <- function(params, species, n_total = 1e5) {     sp <- species_params(params); s <- sp$species == species; sps <- sp[s, ]     w <- params@w; dens <- params@initial_n[s, ] * getFMort(params)[s, ]     l_max <- (sps$w_max / sps$a)^(1 / sps$b)     bins  <- seq(floor((min(w[dens > 0]) / sps$a)^(1 / sps$b)), floor(l_max) - 1)     rate  <- model_catch_rate(params, species, bins)     bins  <- bins[rate > 0]; rate <- rate[rate > 0]     count <- round(rate / sum(rate) * n_total)     data.frame(species = species, gear = "total", length = bins[count > 0],                dl = 1, catch = count[count > 0]) }  # The model's predicted catch density (a PDF) over given length bins. model_catch_pdf <- function(params, species, bins) {     r <- model_catch_rate(params, species, bins)     r / sum(r) }  # Set the diffusion coefficient D_ext and recompute the (diffusion-aware) # steady state, holding mortality, growth and selectivity fixed. set_D_ext <- function(params, species, D) {     sp <- species_params(params); s <- sp$species == species     sp$D_ext[s] <- D; species_params(params) <- sp     params@ext_diffusion[s, ] <- D * params@w^(sp$n[s] + 1)     steadySingleSpecies(params, species = species) }  species <- "Haddock" # Solve the single-species steady state, the spectrum matchCatch() reconstructs, # so the synthetic catch is one the fit's solver can reproduce exactly. p0      <- steadySingleSpecies(make_single_gear(), species = species) s       <- species_params(p0)$species == species sps     <- species_params(p0)[s, ] lengths <- (p0@w / sps$a)^(1 / sps$b)   # length (cm) of each weight bin  # Make the experiment self-consistent: the "observed" yield is this model's own # yield, not the celtic multispecies value carried over by make_single_gear(). # The catch shape barely constrains the mortality, so an inconsistent yield # target would pull the recovered mortality off the truth. gp0 <- gear_params(p0); gi0 <- which(gp0$species == species) gp0$yield_observed[gi0] <- getYield(p0)[s] gear_params(p0) <- gp0

title: Incorporating predation diffusion
text: Let us assume prey abundance given power law: \(N_c(w)=N_0w^{-\lambda}\) predation kernel \[ \phi(w/w_p) = \exp\left(-\frac{\log(w/w_p/\beta)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right). \tag{4}\] juveniles \(\psi(w)=0\) hence integral expression Eq. 2 growth rate becomes \[ \begin{split} I_g&:=\int N_c(w_p)\phi(w/w_p)\alpha\,(1-\psi(w)) w_p\,dw_p\\ &=\alpha\int w_p^{1-\lambda}\exp\left(-\frac{\log(w/w_p/\beta)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)dw_p. \end{split} \tag{5}\] integral can evaluated easily changing integration variable \(x=\log(w_p/w_0)\)arbitrary reference weight \(w_0\) recognising resulting integral \[ I_g=\alpha\, w_0^{2-\lambda}\int e^{(2-\lambda)x}\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\log(w/w_0)+\log(\beta))^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)dx \tag{6}\] Gaussian integral. Using general result \[ \int e^{ax}\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)dx = \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\sigma^2}}\exp\left(\mu+\frac{^2\sigma^2}{2}\right) \tag{7}\] \(= 2-\lambda\) \(\mu = \log(w/w_0)-\log(\beta)\) find \[ \begin{split} I_g&= \alpha\, w_0^{2-\lambda}\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\sigma^2}}\exp\left((2-\lambda)(\log(w/w_0)-\log(\beta))+\frac{(2-\lambda)^2\sigma^2}{2}\right)\\ &=\alpha w^{2-\lambda}\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\sigma^2}}\beta^{\lambda - code: growthControlUI <- function(p, input) {     sp <- p@species_params[input$sp, ]     tagList(         sliderInput("gamma", "Search volume coefficient 'gamma'",                     value = sp$gamma,                     min = signif(sp$gamma / 2, 3),                     max = signif(sp$gamma * 1.5, 3),                     step = sp$gamma / 50, ticks = FALSE)     ) }  growthControl <- function(input, output, session, params, params_old, flags, ...) {     observeEvent(input$gamma, {         p <- params()         sp <- input$sp         # Skip the first fire after a species switch (see "The flags pattern")         if (!identical(sp, flags$sp_old_pred)) {             flags$sp_old_pred <- sp             return()         }         p@species_params[sp, "gamma"] <- input$gamma         p <- setSearchVolume(p)         tuneParams_update_species(sp, p, params, params_old)     },     ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE) } if (!identical(sp, flags$sp_old_pred)) {     flags$sp_old_pred <- sp     return() } intakeControlUI <- function(p, input) {     sp <- p@species_params[input$sp, ]     tagList(         sliderInput("h", "Max intake coefficient 'h'",                     value = sp$h,                     min = signif(sp$h / 2, 3),                     max = signif(sp$h * 1.5, 3),                     step = sp$h / 50, ticks = FALSE)     ) }  intakeControl <- function(input, output, session, params, params_old, flags, ...) {     observeEvent(input$h, {         p <- params()         sp <- input$sp         if (!identical(sp, flags$sp_old_intake)) {             flags$sp_old_intake <- sp             return()         }         p@species_params[sp, "h"] <- input$h         p <- setMaxIntakeRate(p)         tuneParams_update_species(sp, p, params, params_old)     },     ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE) }  # what: Von Bertalanffy growth in length and weight
title: A mizer model with von Bertalanffy growth
text: von Bertalanffy model describes growth length \(l\) \[ \frac{dl}{dt} = k_{vb}\,(L_\infty - l), \qquad l(t) = L_\infty\left(1 - e^{-k_{vb}(t - t_0)}\right), \tag{1}\] \(L_\infty\) asymptotic length, \(k_{vb}\) growth rate constant \(t_0\) (hypothetical) age length zero. Mizer works terms weight \(w\), related length allometric law \(w = \,l^{b}\), asymptotic weight \(w_\infty = \,L_\infty^{b}\). convenient introduce variable \[ u = w^{1/b} = ^{1/b}\, l , \qquad u_\infty = w_\infty^{1/b} = ^{1/b}\, L_\infty , \] simply length constant factor \(^{1/b}\). \(u\) proportional \(l\), satisfies linear equation, \[ \frac{du}{dt} = k_{vb}\,(u_\infty - u), \qquad u(t) = u_\infty\left(1 - e^{-k_{vb}(t - t_0)}\right). \tag{2}\] Transforming back weight \(w = u^{b}\) \(\frac{dw}{dt} = b\,u^{b-1}\frac{du}{dt}\), using \(u^{b-1} = w^{\,1-1/b}\), gives von Bertalanffy growth rate weight, \[ \frac{dw}{dt} = g_{vb}(w) = \,w^{n} - B\,w \] \[ n = 1 - \frac1b,\quad = b\,k_{vb}\,w_\infty^{1/b},\quad B = b\,k_{vb}. \tag{3}\] growth rate returned vonBertalanffyGrowth(). positive \(w < w_\infty\) vanishes \(w = w_\infty\), \(\,w_\infty^{n} = B\,w_\infty\). exponent relation \(n = 1 - 1/b\) ties mizer growth exponent weight–length exponent \(b\).

code: # Illustrative parameters (a mildly negative t0, so the constant-factor # speed-up is feasible and its discontinuity can be shown cleanly). b <- 3; k <- 0.38; w_inf <- 430; t0 <- -0.3; w_mat <- 69; w_min <- 1e-3 n <- 1 - 1 / b A <- b * k * w_inf^(1 / b); B <- b * k uf <- function(w) w^(1 / b) u_inf <- uf(w_inf); u_mat <- uf(w_mat); u_min <- uf(w_min)  g_vb <- function(w) A * w^n - B * w t_mat <- t0 - log(1 - u_mat / u_inf) / k  # constant-factor speed-up: solve for c age_c <- function(c) log((u_inf - c * u_min) / (u_inf - c * u_mat)) / (c * k) c_star <- uniroot(function(c) age_c(c) - t_mat, c(1e-8, 1))$root g_const <- function(w) ifelse(w < w_mat, A * w^n - c_star * B * w, g_vb(w))  # tapering speed-up: Delta = s * w^n * (1 - (w / w_mat)^(1 - n)), solve for s. # g_vb + Delta is again a von Bertalanffy form, so the age has a closed form. Delta <- function(w, s) ifelse(w < w_mat, s * w^n * (1 - (w / w_mat)^(1 - n)), 0) age_s <- function(s) {     A_t <- A + s; B_t <- B + s / u_mat; k_t <- B_t / b   # modified vB coefficients     log((A_t / B_t - u_min) / (A_t / B_t - u_mat)) / k_t } s_star <- uniroot(function(s) age_s(s) - t_mat, c(0, 1e5))$root g_taper <- function(w) g_vb(w) + Delta(w, s_star)  w <- seq(w_min, 1.6 * w_mat, length.out = 600) plot(w, g_vb(w), type = "l", col = "grey70", lwd = 6,      xlab = "weight w", ylab = "growth rate dw/dt",      ylim = c(0, max(g_const(w)))) lines(w, g_const(w), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2, lty = 2) lines(w, g_taper(w), col = "steelblue", lwd = 2) abline(v = w_mat, col = "grey40", lty = 3) text(w_mat, 0, expression(w[mat]), pos = 4, col = "grey40") legend("topleft", bty = "n",        col = c("grey70", "firebrick", "steelblue"),        lwd = c(6, 2, 2), lty = c(1, 2, 1),        legend = c("von Bertalanffy", "constant speed-up (discontinuous)",                   "tapering speed-up (continuous)"))

title: Building a Mizer version of an Ecopath model
text: typical workflow creating mizer model Ecopath data involves following steps: Export Ecopath Parameters: Open Ecopath model “Ecopath Ecosim” export parameters CSV files. Prepare Species Table: Create table R one row species want include mizer model. table must contain: species: name species. w_max: largest observed size species. w_mat: weight maturity. ecopath_groups: corresponding Ecopath group(s). Initialize Model: Use newAllometricParams() create mizer model based parameters. sets model allometric encounter mortality rates, initially interactions. Match Observations: Use various functions provided package matchBiomass() match total biomass species, matchGrowth() match growth rates, matchCatch() match total yield size distribution catch, matchConsumption() match total consumption species. Tune Model: Use interactive Shiny gadget tuneEcopath() fine-tune model reproduce observed size structure Ecopath parameters. gadget allows interactively adjust parameters see effects growth, yield, consumption real-time. Set predation preferences: Use matchDiet() set predation preferences model match observed diet compositions.

title: Get diffusion rate — getDiffusion
text: diffusion rate \(d_i(w)\) species \(\) weight \(w\) contributions encounter fish prey resource. determined summing prey species resource spectrum integrating prey sizes \(w_p\), weighted predation kernel \(\phi(w,w_p)\): $$ d_i(w) = (1-f_i(w))(\alpha_i(1-\psi_i(w)))^2\gamma_i(w) \int \left( \theta_{ip} N_R(w_p) + \sum_{j} \theta_{ij} N_j(w_p) \right) \phi_i(w,w_p) w_p^2 \, dw_p. $$ \(N_j(w)\) abundance density species \(j\) \(N_R(w)\) abundance density resource. overall prefactor \(\gamma_i(w)\) determines predation power predator. interpreted search volume set mizer::setSearchVolume() function. predation kernel \(\phi(w,w_p)\) set mizer::setPredKernel() function. species interaction matrix \(\theta_{ij}\) set mizer::setInteraction() resource interaction vector \(\theta_{ip}\) taken interaction_resource column params@species_params. \(f(w)\) feeding level calculated mizer::getFeedingLevel(). \(\psi(w)\) proportion available energy invested reproduction instead growth, stored params@psi.
